measurement_process: Separate Python3 process on k3s host, outside API/OTP containers, read-only source ZIP access. No production index built.

representation.geometry: Shared full GTFS shapes, dict shape_id -> array<double>[lon,lat,shape_dist_traveled,...]. No per-edge geometry copies. This is a storage measurement, not a claim that different full shape IDs are physical edge variants.
representation.schedules: Not retained. External disk index is a separate task/dependency.

limits: No full road cache, spatial index, route matching scratch arrays or concurrent request working sets measured.
Logical object byte counts and process RSS are different measures; freed Python objects may leave resident allocator memory.
Geometry representation is an explicit compact array assumption; Python dict per point would be much larger.
All GTFS stops/shapes counted; auxiliary graph is not the complete OTP routing graph.
Peak RSS includes measurement overhead from recursive deep-size accounting; it is a conservative process peak, not isolated graph-payload size.

cluster_snapshot.snapshot_scope: kubectl top pods and free -m before measurement; point-in-time values

interpretation.answer: The measured auxiliary stop graph fits comfortably in node RAM; fitting it in the current API pod is plausible, but total 512MiB safety also depends on unmeasured request scratch space, spatial index and bounded traffic cache.
interpretation.disk_index: Explicit external dependency. No production disk index was created.
